newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ahold Brazil deal surprising and daring - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Ahold Brazil deal surprising and daring - analysts.

text.p: Dutch supermarket giant Ahold's move into Latin America through a joint venture with Brazilian food retailer Bompreco caught analysts off guard on Monday.
"We had been looking for further expansion through joint ventures, but not in Brazil," said John David Roeg, retail analyst with Bank Labouchere.
"It's a surprising and daring move," said ING Barings' Dennis Jullens. "With this step, Ahold has gained a foothold in Latin America's biggest and most developed market".
Ahold said earlier it had signed a letter of intent to acquire a 50 percent stake in Bompreco, Brazil's fourth-biggest food retailer with annual sales of some $1.4 billion.
Jullens said the move represented yet another step towards fulfilling Ahold's ambitions of becoming one of the world's leading retailers.

He said the deal was unlikely to have a negative impact on earnings per share. "Ahold is very much aware of shareholders' value, and the extra income generated through Stop & Shop in the second half gives the company some leeway for new acquisitions," he said.
Jullens said he expected Ahold's recent acquisition of U.S. supermarket chain Stop & Shop to boost its bottom line by some $150 million in the 1996 second half.
Labouchere's Roeg was a little less enthusiastic, given that the move signalled a diversification into consumer credit for Ahold.
"Ahold does not have any experience in financing," he said. "It could turn out very profitable but it's also a bit risky."
Bompreco runs a customer loyalty programme, offering customers a credit card which can also be used in some 16,000 third-party retail outlets in north eastern Brazil.
